CANNON-RECOIL STARBOARD — Manning the starboard sky-cannon mid-recoil at the cannon-port, brass breech kicking back against her braced shoulder, smoke blooming thick from the muzzle, spent brass shell spinning past her boot, coat-tails whipped horizontal by the blast-wind, hair slashing across her jaw, the enemy frigate looming closer through the dissipating smoke.

BOARDING-LEAP TWIN-PISTOLS — Leaping from the gunwale mid-dogfight, both boots leaving the brass rail simultaneously, twin brass pistols raised at opposing angles, coat fully streaming behind her, the gap between hulls yawning below her, cannon-flash from the enemy deck lighting her from beneath, hair flung wild across her face.

BRIDGE-SHOUT COURSE-CORRECTION — Shouting course-corrections through a brass speaking-tube while leaning hard over the chart-table on the bridge, brass quill still gripped in her free hand trailing ink, gas-lit amber gauges glowing behind her, dividers skidding on the chart as the ship heels into the turn she just ordered.

RIGGING-CLIMB STORM-REPAIR — Climbing the dirigible-rigging mid-storm to reach a torn fin-panel, brass-handled wrench clamped between her teeth, one gauntleted hand locking around the wet cable, lightning forking past the dirigible-spine a yard behind her, hair fully torn loose and streaming upward, the fin flapping one more gust from shearing away.

PROW-PISTOL BOARDER-SHOT — Firing a brass-plated pistol from the prow rigging at a boarder already mid-leap across the gap, muzzle-flash scorching the rigging-rope beside her cheek, brass shell ejecting in a bright arc, her body twisted around the rope one-handed, the boarder's trajectory still carrying him forward regardless.

SPOTTER-PLATFORM SWEEP — Leaning bodily into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, brass spyglass extended fully, coat-tails gone horizontal, her free hand white-knuckled on the platform strut, the deck impossibly small below, an enemy silhouette she has just spotted cresting the cloud-bank ahead and bearing hard to port.

CUTLASS-PARRY GUNWALE — Parrying a sky-cutlass blow on the gunwale with her brass-handled cutlass, sparks raking off the meeting blades, her free hand braced on the brass railing behind her, knees bent under the force of the strike, the boarder already torquing his shoulder for the second swing.

WHEEL-AND-GLASS COMMAND — Gripping the helm with one hand and a brass spyglass with the other, body torqued sideways to read the closing enemy bearing while steering, the wheel pulling against her palm, hair whipping across the lens, her helmsman reaching for the wheel she has not yet released.

FUSE-LIGHTING CANNON — Crouching beside the starboard cannon at the cannon-port, brass match touched to the fuse, the spark already hissing along the cord toward the breech, her face turned aside and eyes narrowed against the coming flash, the enemy hull filling the port-opening behind her.

RIGGING-SWING PISTOLS-DRAWN — Swinging on a rigging-line between two ships mid-dogfight, both brass pistols leveled outward, boots skimming past the enemy ship's rail by inches, coat bellowing, the line at its arc-peak and about to carry her back unless she releases now, muzzle-flash already pulsing from her right hand.

SIGNAL-LANTERN GUNWALE — Holding a brass-and-glass signal-lantern high from the gunwale, body braced sideways against the rail as the ship rolls, amber flame-light washing across her upturned face, her free hand locked on the shroud-line, the distant sister-ship emerging through cloud-haze and beginning to alter course in answer.

GRENADE-THROW BOARDING-GAP — Throwing a brass-shelled grenade across the gap between hulls at boarding-range, arm fully extended at release, her body pivoting at the waist from the throw, coat swirling around her legs, the grenade already turning end-over-end in the void between the two ships and the enemy deck-crew scattering below it.

CHART-TABLE COURSE-PLOT — Sweeping a brass quill across the chart-table mid-calculation, her other hand pressing the chart flat against the slipstream bleeding through the bridge-port, amber gauges spiking behind her as altitude drops, the brass dividers skidding from her elbow, the storm-front she is racing visible through the glass ahead.

ASTROLABE EYE CLOUD-COVER — Reading a brass astrolabe held to her eye from the spotter-platform, body angled hard against the slipstream, cloud-cover pressing in from both sides, one boot hooked around the platform strut for purchase, the instrument's rings clicking against her brow, the bearing she needs seconds from resolving or being lost in cloud.

SPAR-SPRINT CUTLASS-RAISED — Sprinting along the spar with a sky-cutlass raised overhead, arms pumping for balance on the narrow beam, coat streaming flat behind her, the spar flexing under each running step, a boarder sprinting toward her from the other end and the gap between them closing to one stride.

ENGINE-VALVE WRENCH-SWING — Swinging a brass-handled wrench at a misfiring engine-valve in the mid-section engineering bay, both hands on the handle, teeth gritted, sparks spitting from the seized fitting and catching in her hair, the engine's rhythm stuttering dangerously, the whole gondola shuddering as she strikes it a second time.

PROW-DIVE CLINGING — Clinging to the prow-rail as the ship noses into a steep dive, her body nearly horizontal, boots locked around the lower strut, coat streaming straight up past her face, hair a vertical column above her head, the cloud-layer rushing up at speed and the altimeter behind her spinning freely.

SEMAPHORE-HAUL SIGNAL — Hauling a semaphore flag-set through a complex code sequence at the signal-station on the upper deck, arms at two different flag-angles simultaneously, shoulders driving the motion, the flags snapping taut in the slipstream, her body braced wide against the deck-roll, the receiving ship beginning to acknowledge through the haze.

ROPE-HAUL LISTING-SHIP — Hauling on a heavy line to right a listing ship from the port rail, her entire body angled back at forty-five degrees, boots braced against the canted deck-planking, gloved hands hand-over-hand on the hawser, rope-fibers sparking with friction, the horizon tilting in the wrong direction as the list deepens before it corrects.

SIGNAL-FLARE BRASS-PISTOL — Firing a signal-flare from a brass-handled pistol from the gunwale, the flare already corkscrewing skyward in red smoke above her raised arm, muzzle-bloom lighting the underside of the clouds pink, her other hand locked on the shroud, coat-tail catching the updraft from the discharge, a sister-ship below still dark and unaware.

BOARDER-PARRY SECOND-STRIKE — Absorbing a boarder's second cutlass-strike with her blade crossed hard at the cannon-port, the impact driving her back heel against the brass breach-housing, sparks cascading between the locked blades, her free elbow already cocking for a counter-strike, a second boarder swinging in on a line just over the first man's shoulder.

MESSENGER-BIRD RELEASE — Releasing a mechanical messenger-bird from a brass cage at the bridge-rail, both hands splayed open at release, the bird's brass wings catching mid-deployment, gears audible through the wind-roar, her body leaning forward after it, coat blown back, the destination ship a faint smudge in the far cloud-gap the bird is already arrowing toward.

VORTEX-BOW STANDING — Standing on the bow mid-vortex with coat streaming horizontally and both hands locked on the prow-rail, hair a near-horizontal banner, the ship's nose yawing against the rotational pull, spray and cloud-matter stinging her face sideways, her weight thrown entirely onto one rail-grip as the deck tilts hard to starboard.

CANNON-FUSE BRASS-MATCH — Touching a brass match to the fuse at the port-side cannon mid-broadside, the spark catching instantly, her head already turning away from the breech, one hand up to shield her ear, the gun-crew frozen in the half-second before the world comes apart, enemy rigging visible through the smoke directly in the cannon's line.

RAIL-LEAN SISTER-SHIPS — Leaning far over the port rail to watch sister-ships peel away in formation below, one hand locked on the shroud, her torso past the rail's center of gravity, hair hanging loose and downward, coat front flapping against the hull-side, the lower ships banking in tight arcs she is about to signal them to break.
